# libraw-wasm (OpenMP)

Drop-in replacement for the published `libraw-wasm@1.6.0`, rebuilt so LibRaw's
demosaic actually uses more than one core. Generated by `tools/build-libraw.sh`;
do not edit anything in `dist/` by hand.

## Why this exists

The published package builds LibRaw with `--enable-openmp` but never puts
`-fopenmp` in `CFLAGS`/`CXXFLAGS`. Autoconf's `AX_OPENMP` probe therefore fails
silently, `_OPENMP` is never defined, `LIBRAW_USE_OPENMP` is never set, and every
`#pragma omp` in LibRaw is preprocessed away. The shipped wasm contains zero
OpenMP symbols, so a 40 MP X-Trans frame demosaics on one core no matter how
many the machine has.

That was not really fixable before: Emscripten only gained an OpenMP runtime in
**6.0.3** (PR emscripten-core/emscripten#27073, July 2026). This build uses
6.0.5, which carries LLVM 22.1.8's libomp.

Two upstream bugs are patched at the same time, both in the embind wrapper:

- **`gamm` was unreachable.** The binding only copied the array when it had
  exactly six elements, while its own TypeScript type declared two and LibRaw
  only reads the first two. `gamm: [1, 1]` — dcraw's "give me linear" idiom —
  was silently discarded, and every decode came back on the default 0.45/4.5
  curve. Now any length from two upwards is accepted.
- **No thread controls.** `maxThreads()` and `setThreads(n)` are added as
  module-level exports and plumbed through `worker.js` and the `LibRaw` class,
  so several decoder instances can share one machine instead of each forming a
  full-width team.

## What the app has to do

Wasm threads need `SharedArrayBuffer`, which the browser only grants a
cross-origin-isolated document. `vite.config.ts` sets `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy:
same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` for dev and
preview; `public/_headers` carries the same pair to static hosts. Without them
`maxThreads()` reports 1 and `src/raw/pool.ts` falls back to banded decoding.

## Rebuilding

```sh
source /path/to/emsdk/emsdk_env.sh          # emsdk >= 6.0.3
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/libtool/libexec/gnubin:$PATH"   # glibtool on macOS
./tools/build-libraw.sh                      # FORCE_LIBS=1 to rebuild LCMS + LibRaw
```

Sources are fetched into `.libraw-build/` (git-ignored) and the result is copied
here. The script fails the build if the linked wasm does not contain the OpenMP
runtime or the `setThreads` binding.
